anomalies.observed: R11 (0 Ω) connects the two servo signal nets directly: Net-(J10-Pin_3) on one side and Net-(J7-Pin_3) on the other. Neither side is a bus pin. Each servo signal reaches its own GPIO only through a separate 1 kΩ series resistor (R18 to /NET0002, R19 to /NET0036).
anomalies.expected: The spec describes R9–R12 as 0 Ω selectors that choose which M5Stack bus pin (19/21 for ch.1, 20/22 for ch.2) drives each PWM line, and says 'Short R9, R11 for others'. In PWM mode the two channels must stay independent. A 0 Ω link between the two servo signal nets is only appropriate for the serial bridge, which the spec places on R13/R14.

evidence.quote: | R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2

anomalies.impact: If the R11 link is populated in PWM mode, the two servo signal lines are shorted together. Both servos then receive the same PWM signal from whichever GPIO drives it, and the two independent PWM channels are lost. In serial mode the same link would also tie the servo lines together, so the jumper's population must match the chosen mode.

parsed.summary: The netlist's R11 is a 0 Ω link between the two servo signal nets, not a bus-pin selector as the spec describes, so populating it in PWM mode would short the two PWM channels together.
